result.summary: RECONSTRUCTED HANDOFF -- written 2026-09-03 after the fact from the run's real, on-disk evidence: the current test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs carries a 'http_transport/4 -- DNS rebinding' describe block (confirmed present at reconstruction time, containing two tests -- one rejecting a hostname resolving to 169.254.169.254 via an injected resolver, one covering the DNS-rebinding scenario itself) whose own header comment cites 'queue task 415, REQ-214 AC2' explicitly, plus a comment stating this coverage was added because 'the seam existed but no such test had been written yet' -- direct, on-disk confirmation this FAIL was real and this exact gap was found. Timestamps are reconstructed approximations. 1 narrow gap: REQ-214's real AC2 (docs/requirements.yaml, independently re-read at reconstruction time) requires 'a dispatch row whose rendered URL resolves to a blocked SSRF range... and a DNS-rebinding case via an injected resolver, mirroring test/letflow/webhooks/url_validator_test.exs's own three cases' -- the real file at that path (test/letflow/webhooks/url_validator_test.exs, confirmed to exist at this exact path, not the lib/ path an earlier draft of this task assumed) has three resolver-injected rejection cases (loopback 127.0.0.1, private RFC-1918 10.0.0.1, and a rebinding-shaped case at 169.254.169.254 -- all via an injected resolver fn). At this point in the run, rework2 had just added the http_transport/3->4 split (the seam), but no test yet exercised it for a DNS-rebinding-shaped rejection specifically -- rework2's own new tests covered the genuine :advance and genuine retriable-failure paths, not this SSRF-rejection-via-injected-resolver case. Independently re-verified everything else: re-ran the file directly (39 tests at this point, all passing), re-mapped every other REQ-214 AC to real assertions read directly (not trusted from test/specs/REQ-214.md alone, which did not yet exist at this point in the run), and independently re-ran 2 of the 6 mutations TEST-DESIGNER's step-03 report claimed to have tried -- both still caught by the current test suite. Test isolation re-confirmed (setup-based tenant fixtures, no setup_all, no shared mutable state).
